newsitem.title: USA: Leave US farm bill alone--Senate Ag chairman Lugar.
newsitem.headline: Leave US farm bill alone--Senate Ag chairman Lugar.

text.p: U.S. Senate Agriculture Committee chairman Richard Lugar warned Wednesday that any attempt for major revisions in the "Freedom to Farm" law could trigger a new attack on farm subsidies.
In an interview with Reuters, Lugar said it was unlikely he would take aim at the sugar or peanut supports in 1997. The Indiana Republican tried to scale back supports in the past.
"My own view is...probably we should leave the farm bill alone," Lugar said.
"If others are interested in a gross assault on the farm bill, I may have enthusiams of my own..."
American agriculture "does not want another full-scale" fight over farm policy, he added.
Populist Democrats have said they hoped to replace the 1996 farm law with a different plan, such as marketing loans.
Lugar, who was a strong advocate of the "Freedom to Farm" law, said the law appeared to be working well and to be popular among farmers.
Although President Clinton has said he would seek changes in the federal safety net for farmers, Lugar said "there does not appear to be a large push from the administration" for major change.
"I am hopeful we can work with them objectively" in monitoring implementation of the farm law and reorganization of the mammoth Agriculture Department, which began two years ago.

Lugar said his agenda for the new session of Congress included further work on alternative fuels, examination of so-called risk management tools for farmers and reauthorization of U.S. agricultural research programs He
said one of his first priorities would be passage of a bill to revise the Commodity Exchange Act.
